themes.title: Canada-US trade war LIVE — Section 338 50% tariffs operative since Aug 22; Canada 700+ line retaliation effective Sept 8 (7 days); talks collapsed; Trump 50% auto tariff threat Jan 1 2027
themes.summary: As of September 1, the Canada-US trade war is at maximum escalation with Canada's September 8 retaliatory tariff effective date now seven days away and no diplomatic channel open. The US Section 338 50% tariffs on approximately $27.6 billion of Canadian goods have been operative since August 22 — covering dairy, alcohol, building materials, electronics, apparel, and agricultural goods — and notably apply even to CUSMA-compliant goods with no statutory expiry. Canada's government confirmed on August 25 a dollar-for-dollar retaliation covering over 700 tariff lines (C$27.6 billion in US imports), with rates of 15%, 25%, and 50% matched to US Section 338 and Section 232 rates. Sectors targeted include steel and aluminum (duties doubled to 50%), dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, effective 12:01 a.m. September 8. Trade negotiations collapsed on the night of August 21-22, with both sides trading blame: USTR Greer said Canada had 'declined to finalize the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week,' while PM Carney said the US proposed terms that were 'uneconomic, unfair, and undermined the net benefits for Canada.' Carney declared Canada was 'at war' and said the government would introduce additional support measures on top of the nearly $25 billion already provided over 18 months. The September 8 binary remains the live tripwire: the question is whether Washington responds to Canada's retaliation with a counter-escalation (Greer had previously signalled willingness to respond) or absorbs it. Trump's separate threat to impose 50% tariffs on all Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel effective January 1, 2027 adds a structural medium-term CAD negative beyond the immediate Sept 8 catalyst. USDCAD is in the 1.39 area, probing topside on the dual tailwind of CAD structural weakness from the tariff shock and USD strength from the Warsh hawkish repricing (CME FedWatch now at 66% for a Sep hike). The combination of Section 338 tariffs with no expiry and Canada's commitment to a 'focused response' points to a prolonged dispute rather than a near-term resolution.

implications.CAD: MAXIMUM CAD negative — US 50% tariffs live since Aug 22, full 700+ line retaliation list published with Sept 8 effective date, negotiations explicitly collapsed, Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat adds structural overhang. USDCAD ~1.39, approaching/probing key 1.3900. BoC rate hike expectations further compressed as tariff growth drag dominates. Sept 8 is the next hard catalyst: US counter-retaliation = USDCAD accelerates above 1.40; US silence/absorption = modest near-term CAD relief but structural weakness remains. Dual tariff shock (US 50% on CAD goods + CAD 15-50% retaliation raising input costs for Canadian industry) amplifies growth damage beyond the direct export hit.
implications.USD: USDCAD directionally bullish from tariff shock, reinforced by post-Warsh hawkish USD repricing (CME FedWatch 66% Sep hike). Canada tariff shock adds modest USD safe-haven bid vs commodity bloc.
implications.MXN: USMCA credibility damage from US-Canada rupture keeps uncertainty elevated on the US-Mexico track. Modest USDMXN risk premium from contagion.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD likely bid on CAD weakness. Broader protectionism signal from Section 338 invocation has limited but non-zero EUR contagion.
implications.AUD: Commodity-bloc contagion — AUD trades defensively in acute CAD-shock episodes. AUDUSD subject to additional headwind from post-Warsh USD strength; vulnerable to further risk-off from US-Canada escalation spiral post Sept 8.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol elevated. NZD defensive in commodity-bloc risk-off episodes.
implications.GBP: GBPCAD directional trade on CAD weakness. GBP otherwise dominated by BoE path and post-Warsh USD dynamics.
implications.JPY: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus structural JPY bid from BOJ Sep hike cycle.

themes.watchLevel: USDCAD 1.3900 is the immediate live test — a clean daily close above 1.3900 opens 1.4017-1.4021 (50-day EMA area) and then 1.4100. Post-Warsh USD tailwind (66% Sep hike odds on CME) makes 1.40 a plausible near-term target absent a diplomatic surprise. USDCAD 1.3800-1.3820 is near-term downside support; a close below 1.3780 would require a surprise diplomatic reopening. Sept 8 Canada retaliation effective date: US counter-retaliation = USDCAD accelerates above 1.40; US silence/absorption = modest near-term CAD relief rally toward 1.3850. Jan 1 2027 automotive tariff threat (50% on all Canadian cars, trucks, parts) is a structural medium-term CAD negative even if Sept 8 passes without escalation. Theme ends only on: (1) formal re-opening of US-Canada talks with credible framework, or (2) Trump executive action suspending Section 338.

themes.title: BOJ Sep 17-18 hike ~80% priced + intervention regime — Tokyo CPI core-core hit 2.0%; MUFG forecasts Sep + Jan 2027 double-hike; USDJPY holding near 159-160; Takata speech Sep 2 tomorrow
themes.summary: As of September 1, the BOJ September 17-18 rate hike narrative remains firmly intact and the intervention regime is actively defending the 160.00 level. USDJPY briefly touched 160.00 during August 29 overseas trading driven by the post-Warsh hawkish USD repricing that added 12bps to the US 2yr yield. Reuters sources confirmed the BOJ is set to raise rates as soon as September and is likely to hike more aggressively than its prior roughly twice-yearly pace — a shift reflecting concerns over price pressures from Middle East-related energy costs, strong global AI demand, and persistent JPY weakness. One Reuters source stated 'an early rate hike has come into sight,' and another echoed that 'the BOJ could also accelerate the pace of rate increases.' MUFG's global and Japan teams forecast two hikes: September 2026 and January 2027, which underpins their USD/JPY lower view through 160. The Tokyo CPI print on August 28 was a key catalyst: core-core (ex-fresh food and energy, the BOJ's preferred underlying measure) accelerated to 2.0% YoY — hitting the BOJ's 2% inflation target directly for the first time in this cycle. BOJ is expecting core inflation to surge above 2% in the second half of fiscal 2026, with July producer prices growing 7.1% YoY. The US-Japan joint intervention regime, which involved Japan spending approximately $58.97 billion in end-July operations that drove USDJPY to 155.27 — the first US-Japan coordinated FX action since 2011 — remains structurally intact but is not actively firing. The Kyodo news agency reported that the BOJ's September hike signal was precisely what led the US to join the intervention, tying the regime's credibility to policy follow-through. Analysts note that 'intervention can buy time, but the heavy lifting will fall on BOJ normalization as early as September.' The critical upcoming event is the Takata speech on September 2 (tomorrow) — Takata dissented at the July meeting in favour of raising rates immediately to 1.25% and is the most hawkish board member. Any explicit September hike endorsement from Takata would be a significant JPY catalyst. Next calendar events: Takata speech Sep 2, Masu speech Sep 10, BOJ Sep 17-18 meeting (hard binary). BOJ current rate is 1.00% (June hike); Sep hike would take it to 1.25%.

implications.JPY: Three-pillar structural JPY support in cross-current with post-Warsh USD strength: (1) Intervention regime — dry powder preserved, credibility tested by 160 touch; (2) BOJ Sep hike ~80% priced, Tokyo core-core at 2.0% cements hike case, Reuters/MUFG confirm; (3) Fed rate differential narrowing from BOJ side even as Warsh hawkish repricing partially restores USD yield support. Net: intervention threat and Sep 17-18 BOJ hike binary still dominate medium-term USDJPY direction lower; post-Warsh USD strength + 66% CME Fed hike odds add near-term upside pressure. 160.00 is the live line in the sand for MoF/BOJ coordination.
implications.USD: USDJPY topside meets intervention threat at 160; post-Warsh hawkish repricing (66% Sep hike, DXY ~99.68+) is the dominant near-term USD driver across pairs. Rate differential direction of travel remains USD-negative vs JPY from both sides over medium term but near-term USD support restored.
implications.EUR: EURJPY under pressure from intervention mechanism and BOJ hike pricing. EURUSD dynamics primarily driven by Warsh/Fed repricing.
implications.GBP: GBPJPY under dual intervention and carry-unwind pressure. GBPUSD subject to post-Warsh USD strength.
implications.CHF: CHFJPY lower on intervention pressure. SNB in easing mode.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ hike cycle.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY under intervention pressure. AUDUSD reversed multi-month highs on post-Warsh USD strength.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under intervention pressure; NZDUSD retraced from recent highs on post-Warsh USD strength.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY 160.00 is the LIVE critical line — briefly touched Aug 29, the clearest stress test of the intervention regime in four weeks. A daily close above 160 without MoF verbal or actual intervention signals carry traders have overpowered the regime. Takata speech Sep 2 (TOMORROW): Takata is the most hawkish board member — any explicit Sep hike endorsement = renewed JPY bid, USDJPY pressured toward 157-158. USDJPY below 158.00 = intervention credibility reasserting. USDJPY below 155.27 (post-intervention low) = regime decisively winning. Masu speech Sep 10 is the final pre-meeting BOJ communication. BOJ Sep 17-18 is the hard binary: hike to 1.25% = USDJPY likely drops toward 155-152; no hike = JPY sells off sharply, 160+ re-test, intervention regime faces acute stress. Any MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately.

themes.title: Warsh hawkish at Jackson Hole Aug 28 — Sep hike odds upgraded to 66% on CME FedWatch (was 57.5%); BofA calls 'onus on Warsh to deliver'; next events: Sep 4 payrolls, Sep 11 CPI, Sep 16 FOMC
themes.summary: As of September 1, the Warsh hawkish repricing from Jackson Hole has continued to build rather than fade, with CME FedWatch now showing a 66% probability of a September 16 hike — up from 57.5% immediately post-speech on August 28 and from under 40% pre-speech. The Jackson Hole keynote on August 28 delivered a clearer inflation-fighting signal than the 69% consensus for a neutral tone had anticipated: Warsh noted the PCE price index 'stands at 3.7 percent' over 12 months and '4.1 percent' over six months — both 'well above the 2% target' — and described these figures as 'concerning.' He stated that 'underlying inflation is not slowing' and reiterated he 'would be hard pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive,' implying the case for moving to a more restrictive stance. Bank of America economist Aditya Bhave concluded: 'Absent a material downside surprise, the onus is now on Warsh to deliver a September hike.' BofA holds a call for three hikes ahead, saying Warsh's Jackson Hole speech showed markets 'a more credible Fed.' Governor Lisa Cook has separately noted that headline and core inflation for 2026 are running about 1 percentage point higher than expected, driven by core goods prices rising at a 5% annual pace, reinforcing the hawkish stance. The backdrop includes: the July FOMC vote was 9-3 to hold (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan dissented for a hike, the most dissents since September 2016); the June dot plot showed nine members projecting at least one hike in 2026. Warsh's refusal to pre-commit ('I stand here today committed to a discipline, not to a decision') and his emphasis on trends rather than isolated data points means the Sep 11 August CPI print is the critical near-term tiebreaker. A Chicago PMI miss (47.1 vs 57.9 expected) on August 28 created a growth caution counterpoint, with Sep 4 ISM Manufacturing and payrolls the next growth-side check. The September 16 FOMC meeting with updated SEP and dot plot is the hard policy binary. Goldman Sachs (Hatzius) continues to expect core CPI and PCE around 0.2% MoM in August and forecasts the FOMC holds, illustrating that the Sep 11 CPI print is genuinely pivotal.

implications.USD: DXY ~99.68+ area, holding post-Warsh hawkish gains. CME FedWatch at 66% Sep hike, a new cycle high for hike odds. Sep 11 CPI is now the fulcrum: hot print (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) = Sep hike fully priced above 75%, DXY targets 100.50-101.00; soft print (core at or below 0.2% MoM, consistent with Goldman base case) = hike odds pull back toward 50%, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00. Sep 16 FOMC dots: 2026 dot at 4.0%+ = full hawkish validation; unchanged dots = sell-the-news USD weakness. DXY sustaining above 100.00 = hawkish repricing fully priced; DXY failing back below 98.50 = markets unwinding Warsh hawkish read.
implications.JPY: Warsh hawkish outcome partially restores rate differential, creating cross-current against BOJ Sep hike narrative. USDJPY touched 160.00 Aug 29 — intervention regime being tested in real time. Net: post-Warsh USD support is a USDJPY upside force, BOJ Sep hike + intervention regime is a USDJPY downside force.
implications.EUR: EURUSD has retraced from 1.1657 toward 1.1500-1.1550 on Warsh hawkish repricing. Sep 11 US CPI and Sep 16 FOMC are the next major EURUSD catalysts. ECB dynamics provide partial offset.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD subject to post-Warsh USD strength. Rate convergence story has partially shifted back in USD's favour. BoE's own path and UK data remain independent GBP drivers.
implications.CAD: Post-Warsh USD strength adds a second tailwind to USDCAD alongside the Section 338 tariff shock. USDCAD probing 1.39. Chicago PMI 47.1 downside miss adds growth caution — stagflation narrative limits how far rate hike pricing can extend.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD partially reversed multi-month highs on Warsh hawkish USD repricing. China demand dynamics and RBA path are independent AUD drivers.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDUSD retraced from recent highs on Warsh USD bid.
implications.CHF: USDCHF lifted by Warsh hawkish repricing. SNB easing mode limits CHF upside. CHF safe-haven bid provides partial offset in risk-off episodes.

themes.watchLevel: Sep 4 ISM Manufacturing + payrolls: weak payrolls or ISM miss (below 48) = stagflation narrative limits hike pricing, DXY loses post-Warsh gains; strong payrolls = cements 66%+ hike odds. Sep 11 August CPI is the critical pre-FOMC tiebreaker: hot print (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) = Sep hike above 75%, DXY toward 100.50-101.00, EURUSD toward 1.1350-1.1450; soft print (core at or below 0.2% MoM per Goldman base case) = hike odds pull back toward 50%, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00. Sep 16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy binary: hike 25bps to 3.75-4.00% = full hawkish validation, DXY toward 101-102, EURUSD below 1.1300; hold with hawkish dots (2026 median above 4.00%) = partial validation, DXY 100-101; hold with unchanged dots = sell-the-news USD weakness, DXY retraces toward 98. DXY closing and sustaining below 98.00 = Warsh hawkish read fully unwound. Chicago PMI downside miss (47.1) on Aug 28 is a growth caution — if Sep 4 payrolls show similar deterioration, stagflation narrative caps how far hike pricing can extend.
